questions.question: A student tests how a wooden block floats in a shallow tray of water and then in a deep swimming pool. What will they observe about how well it floats?
options: It floats much better in the deep pool than in the shallow tray.
It floats better in the shallow tray due to less water pressure.
How well it floats is exactly the same because it does not depend on the depth of the liquid.
It will sink in the deep swimming pool but float in the tray.

questions.question: On Earth, approximately how much force is required to lift a mass of 1 kg?
options: 1 N

questions.question: Which of the following formulas correctly represents how to calculate gravitational force (W)?
options: W = m × g
W = m ÷ g
W = m + g
W = g ÷ m

questions.question: If a spring's extension increases by 2 cm when a 1 N force is added, how much will its extension increase when another equal 1 N force is added?
options: 1 cm
2 cm
4 cm
0.5 cm

questions.question: What is the relationship between the extension of a spring and the force applied to it?
options: The extension is directly proportional to the force applied.
The extension is inversely proportional to the force applied.
The extension is independent of the force applied.
The extension decreases as the force applied increases.

questions.question: Why is a metal spring classified as an elastic material?
options: It is very shiny and can conduct electricity well.
It returns to its original length when the force stretching it is removed.
It permanently deforms as soon as any small force is applied.
It breaks easily when a pulling force is applied.

questions.question: What is one major advantage of using a lever when trying to move a heavy load?
options: It can multiply a small force into a larger force.
It completely eliminates the effect of gravity on the load.
It decreases the distance needed to lift the load.
It converts chemical energy directly into electrical energy.

questions.question: Which equation is used to calculate pressure?
options: Pressure = force × area
Pressure = area ÷ force
Pressure = force ÷ area
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit of pressure 'newtons per square metre'?
options: Joule
Watt
Pascal
Newton

questions.question: Why does a boat with a very wide hull have a greater maximum upthrust than a narrow boat of the same weight?
options: The bigger surface area of the hull allows a bigger upthrust to act on it.
The larger surface area increases the gravitational pull on the boat.
The wide hull decreases the volume of water displaced.
Wide boats are made of lighter materials.

questions.question: Why does pressure in a liquid increase as you dive deeper?
options: The temperature of the water increases at greater depths.
There is more liquid pushing down from above.
The density of the liquid decreases rapidly with depth.
Gravitational force is significantly stronger at the bottom of a pool.

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure reduce as you climb higher up a mountain?
options: There is less air pushing down from above.
The temperature of the air is much lower.
Wind speeds are higher at high altitudes.
The Earth's gravity becomes zero at mountain peaks.

questions.question: How does the extension of a rubber band behave when equal-sized increases in force are applied to it?
options: The extension remains absolutely constant for all forces.
The extension increases by the same amount for each equal increase in force.
The extension increases by different amounts for each equal increase in force.
The rubber band does not extend at all when force is applied.

questions.question: When a very heavy box is placed on a floor, what happens to the particles within the floor directly under the box?
options: The particles spread further apart from each other.
The particles disappear and are replaced by air.
The particles are squashed closer together.
The particles start to rotate rapidly in place.

questions.question: How is the moment of a force calculated?
options: Moment = force ÷ perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = force + perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = perpendicular distance ÷ force
